summary: Temporary decryption access to customer transcript shards for privacy validation
description: Issue summary: Privacy Engineering requests time-limited access to KMS-wrapped transcript shards from prod inference logs to validate a customer-initiated GDPR erasure. Justification: Customer claim: residual output appears after requested deletion; Privacy team needs to confirm deletion and identify residual copies. Data requested: Up to 50 transcript shard objects (KMS-wrapped blobs) matching customer_id: cust-90421 and timestamp window 2025-11-01..2026-02-28; prefer hashed identifiers only; no full customer profile. Scope & filters: Only entries with tag 'output-trace-v2' and status='stored'; exclude live session streams; exclude unrelated customers. Access controls & safeguards: Accessors limited to the Privacy Engineering triage group (Ava Martinez, Priya Nair, Tomás Rivera), one-time decryption in a locked ephemeral workstation (bastion) with session recording, immediate re-encryption and zero-copy export only for redaction verification. All work logged and KMS audit entries retained. Approval chain requested: Data Governance -> SRE (KMS owner) -> Legal (if anything resembling PII encountered). Expected turnaround: first response within 48 hours; completion window 5 working days. Risk note: Minimal but includes exposure to raw customer outputs; mitigation via strict scoped filters, on-bastion processing, and deletion of decrypted artifacts after verification. Next steps: SRE to confirm technical feasibility of ephemeral decrypt and advise on required runbook steps; Data Governance to provide written approval; implementers to schedule a 1-hour session with Privacy and SRE.
